{{short description|Japanese mathematician}}
{{Nihongo|'''Tadashi Nakayama'''|中山 正|Nakayama Tadashi|extra=July 26, 1912, [[Tokyo Prefecture]] &ndash; June 5, 1964, [[Nagoya]]}} was a [[mathematician]] who made important contributions to [[representation theory]].

==Career==
He received his degrees from the [[University of Tokyo]] and the [[University of Osaka]] and held permanent positions at the University of Osaka and [[Nagoya University]].  He had visiting positions at [[Princeton University]], [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]], and the [[University of Hamburg]]. [[Nakayama's lemma]], [[Nakayama algebra]]s, [[Nakayama's conjecture]], and the [[Murnaghan–Nakayama rule]] are named after him.
